purpose: Bridge design intelligence to implementation so correct reasoning survives tokens, components, CSS, browser/platform chrome, responsive transformation, motion and runtime rendering.

token_dimensions.rule: Use semantic type roles and optical hierarchy; avoid arbitrary per-screen pixel sizes.
Tune line-height by role and measure; compact UI labels, body reading and editorial display need different rhythms.
Use weight for hierarchy without collapsing every emphasis into bold.
Use a coherent spacing system while permitting optical corrections where geometry alone looks wrong.
Radius is a material/system decision, not a universal decoration applied equally to every container.
Borders establish grouping and state with calibrated contrast; avoid one opaque outline around every object.
Elevation must communicate layering/interaction and remain coherent across light/dark themes.
Brand, neutral and semantic status colors keep distinct ownership.
Density changes information throughput and target ergonomics; compactness must not erase operability.
Duration/easing/spring tokens encode motion families and purpose rather than one global animation recipe.

component_constraints.rule: Interactive components implement idle, hover where applicable, focus, pressed, selected, disabled, loading, error and success states when semantically relevant.
Focus treatment must be visible, theme-compatible and distinct from hover/selection while preserving platform accessibility expectations.
Components survive zero, long, localized, partial, delayed and overflow content.
Menus, popovers, dialogs and tooltips have explicit stacking, dismissal, focus restoration and collision behavior.
Dense desktop controls may be compact visually while maintaining reliable pointer/keyboard targeting and accessibility.
Visual controls bind canonical product actions rather than ad-hoc local handlers with divergent semantics.
Loading and optimistic states prevent duplicate action, stale response and unmount races.
Every semantic state remains legible in light, dark, high-contrast/forced-color and supported custom themes.
Required capability semantics survive layout transformation even when control presentation changes.
Native controls may remain native when intentional; custom styling must pay its accessibility, behavior and maintenance cost.

default_chrome_audit.question: Is native/styled/overlay/reveal behavior intentional, theme-compatible and still operable?
Does the platform/native select fit the product, or does an unstyled default break visual and interaction continuity?
Is native file picking integrated intentionally without leaving a stray browser-default button?
Are browser picker, locale, keyboard and theme behaviors understood rather than cosmetically ignored?
Are steppers, wheel behavior, precision and mobile keyboard behavior intentional?
Are track, thumb, value feedback, focus and touch/keyboard semantics coherent?
Is focus visible and intentional rather than accidentally default, accidentally removed, or visually confused with selection?
Do text/object selection colors preserve legibility and brand/theme semantics?
Is caret visible against editable surfaces and consistent with text/input states?
Are resizable panels/textareas intentionally expressed and discoverable?
Does drag feedback represent the actual object/action rather than an awkward browser snapshot?
Are native validation bubbles compatible with the product's error model, or should validation be owned in-product?
Are custom/native context actions intentional and do essential actions remain reachable elsewhere?
Do arrows, shadows, borders, focus, timing and collision behavior belong to the same material system?
Does cursor shape communicate affordance without becoming decoration?
Are bounce/glow/edge behaviors appropriate to the platform and nested scrolling model?

responsive_rules: Transform hierarchy rather than mechanically stacking every desktop region.
Retain critical actions through alternate surfaces when toolbars or sidebars collapse.
Re-evaluate density, text measure, overlays, sticky regions, tables, canvases and input modality at each meaningful layout regime.
Capture rendered evidence at the smallest supported viewport and at least one wide/high-density workspace condition.
Treat keyboard appearance, safe areas and dynamic viewport changes as state transitions, not fixed breakpoints.

motion_semantics.rule: Motion may teach where an object came from, where it went, or how hierarchy changed; reduced motion preserves that meaning without vestibular transforms.
Feedback should connect user action to result without delaying truth or accepting duplicate activation.
Workspace/canvas navigation may preserve spatial continuity but must remain interruptible and recoverable.
Celebration/ambience is subordinate to task frequency, product tone and consequence; repeated expert actions should not be theatrically slowed.
No animation is a valid high-quality choice when motion would add latency, distraction, ambiguity or fatigue.
Reduced motion is an equivalent semantic branch, not merely duration zero; state hierarchy and acknowledgement remain perceivable.

implementation_rules: Prefer semantic design tokens consumed by components over per-screen magic values.
Prevent CSS transition: all on state-rich controls; name properties and interruption behavior.
Use layout primitives that can express min/max/intrinsic content rather than screenshot-specific fixed geometry.
Measure real font rendering, wrapping and density; design-tool dimensions are hypotheses until browser/runtime rendering confirms them.
Keep z-index and overlay ownership systematic so dialogs, menus, tooltips, command surfaces and canvases cannot arbitrarily out-rank one another.
Style browser chrome only when the behavior remains robust; aesthetic consistency never justifies removing focus, scrolling, selection or platform affordances without an equivalent path.
Performance degradation must remove decoration before it degrades task feedback, input latency or semantic state.
visual_regression_obligations: Capture representative desktop and mobile/small viewport renders for material UI changes.
Compare typography wrap, spacing rhythm, overlay placement, sticky/fixed regions and default-browser chrome, not only pixel percentage.
Review expected deltas manually when anti-aliasing or dynamic content makes raw pixel thresholds noisy.
Include theme/state variants for components whose visual semantics change under dark/high-contrast/error/selected/focus conditions.
Store the accepted baseline revision and test revision so evidence is reproducible.
A passing screenshot diff cannot prove interaction semantics; bind visual evidence to runtime probes for actions, focus and state transitions.
